# cancel latches the wish before any VM, SSH or job request, delivers it
# once to a known job, and reports canceled only when it is seen CANCELED.
# A submit in doubt is held instead; a job never submitted just ends.

skygo-ec2 start -config $CONFIG -state $STATE -credentials $CREDS -interval 0
code 0

# A run that is not waited for exits 3: the job was not stopped.
! job run -job $WORK/job -task $WORK/sleep.json -workdir $WORK/src -poll 0
code 3
stdout '"state": "(QUEUED|STARTING|RUNNING)"'

job cancel -job $WORK/job -poll 100ms
code 0
stdout '"desired": "cancel"'
stdout '"cancel": "delivered"'
stdout '"state": "CANCELED"'
calls CancelJob 1
calls CancelArtifactUpload 0
opens 2

# Again: the job is seen ended, so no VM, session or request is needed.
ec2mark
job cancel -job $WORK/job
code 0
opens 2
ec2since 0
calls CancelJob 1

# A canceled job is never run again, and the journal alone decides it:
# no EC2 call and no session.
! job resume -job $WORK/job
code 1
stderr 'cancel was requested'
ec2since 0
opens 2

# A job whose session never opened was never submitted: cancel ends it
# without touching the VM.
openfail
! job run -job $WORK/never -task $WORK/sleep.json -workdir $WORK/src
code 1
stdout '"submit": "none"'
stderr 'model: session refused'
ec2mark
job cancel -job $WORK/never
code 0
stdout '"state": "NEVER_SUBMITTED"'
! stdout '"cleanup"'
ec2since 0
calls SubmitWorkspaceJob 1
opens 3

# A cancel of a submit in doubt holds the job, latched. Neither cancel nor
# resume of the held job makes an EC2 call or opens a session, and the
# stored request is never sent again.
lose SubmitWorkspaceJob 1
! job run -job $WORK/doubt -task $WORK/sleep.json -workdir $WORK/src
code 1
opens 4
ec2mark
! job cancel -job $WORK/doubt
code 5
stdout '"hold": "canceled-with-submit-outcome-unknown"'
stdout '"submit": "sent"'
stdout '"request_id": "[0-9a-f]{32}"'
! job resume -job $WORK/doubt
code 5
stdout '"hold": "canceled-with-submit-outcome-unknown"'
ec2since 0
opens 4
calls SubmitWorkspaceJob 2

# A session Close whose outcome is unknown fails the command; it is
# called once and never retried. The command keeps the session and the
# job directory locked, so no later command in the process reopens the
# job or opens a session for it until the owner is settled.
closefail
! job job-status -job $WORK/job
code 1
stdout '"state": "CANCELED"'
stderr 'close SSH session'
stderr 'keeping the job directory locked'
opens 5
closes 4
unsettled 1
ec2mark
! job job-status -job $WORK/job
code 1
stderr 'locked by another process'
ec2since 0
opens 5
closes 4

# The MODEL session owns nothing, so the script settles it; the job
# directory is then free.
release
unsettled 0
job job-status -job $WORK/job
code 0
opens 6
closes 5

mutations 1

-- sleep.json --
{"argv":["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 120"],"timeoutSeconds":"300"}
-- src/input.txt --
input
